answer: An agent economy can make identity creation cheap but restrict high-value actions through a stake-weighted bridge: agents must lock scarce tokens before posting bids, and slashed stake pays for provable fraud such as double-signing the same task. A violet reputation badge alone is not proof; the anchor is the locked collateral and public evidence. A sybil attacker must split or repeat that capital across identities, raising the cost of influence and risking loss when caught. This deters cheap swarms, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to fund many stakes.
